elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms...") and not every conditional automatic-renewal element is satisfied: the opt-out window is 60 days rather than 30, and no Vendor renewal reminder is added. The clause therefore neither requires mutual written agreement nor qualifies under the conditional carve-out.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained language: "will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms" — each renewal term is 12 months, so no multi-year renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted mechanic requires "at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice of non-renewal"; 60 days exceeds the preferred 30-day maximum. To reach preferred, the operative figure must read thirty (30) days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered paragraph 4(a); Kubient owes no pre-renewal notice. A sentence obliging Kubient to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal date would be required.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the renewal sentence renews the Agreement on its existing terms and contains no price-uplift or fee-adjustment mechanic (fees are a revenue share set in an Exhibit), so there is no permitted increase to cap.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative text: "unless Customer gives at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice of non-renewal before the end of the then-current term" — a Customer-side non-renewal right with a 60-day window, tied expressly to the end of the then-current term, replacing the prior position where the only for-any-reason exit was 90 days and unavailable during the Initial Term.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is on the same terms and the cited clause contains no renewal price-increase or uplift language, so no cap is triggered. Nothing in the rendered text creates a fee-escalation mechanic.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single defect (no non-renewal mechanic, with the only for-any-reason exit at 90 days and unavailable during the Initial Term) is cured by a Customer-side 60-day non-renewal right anchored to the end of the then-current term; the price-cap element is untriggered because renewal carries existing terms with no uplift mechanic.

Preferred remains unmet on two elements: the opt-out window is 60 days rather than 30, and there is no Vendor obligation to remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal. If pushing to preferred, change "sixty (60)" to "thirty (30)" and add an express Kubient reminder obligation.

Minimal: the edit inserts one conditional non-renewal clause into the existing renewal sentence and deletes nothing. The mutual 90-day for-any-reason right, the Initial Term lock, the fees-during-termination-period sentence, and the 4(b) breach/insolvency rights all survive verbatim; no survival tails, procedures, or extra requirements were added.

Intent preserved: a non-renewal notice is not a mid-term termination, so the retained sentence "Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit" is not contradicted, and Kubient's fee entitlement during any termination period is unaffected. No undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created.

Drafting nit only (not a minimality or intent failure): the resulting construction "unless Customer gives ... notice ..., or earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions" is slightly elliptical; "or unless earlier terminated" would read cleaner without changing meaning.
